Cluster data and build per-cluster networks in one step

Source: R/cluster_data.R
cluster_network.Rd

cluster_network() clusters a set of sequences and estimates one network per cluster in a single call. It runs build_clusters() (dissimilarity clustering with PAM or a hierarchical method) or, with cluster_by = "mmm", build_mmm() (a mixture of Markov chains), then build_network() on each cluster's sequences. The network method is the method given in ...; without one, a netobject input passes on its own method and stored build arguments, so the per-cluster networks are of the same type as the input, and other input gives "relative" transition networks.

The clusters were formed to make the sequences within each one alike, so their networks differ partly by construction. Check the classification with cluster_diagnostics() and the choice of k with cluster_choice() or compare_mmm(), and see how far each cluster's edges move under resampling with bootstrap_network() before reading differences between the networks.

Usage

cluster_network(data, k, cluster_by = "pam", dissimilarity = "hamming", ...)

Arguments

data

The sequences: a data frame, matrix, netobject, bare cograph_network or tna model, as accepted by build_clusters() (or by build_mmm() when cluster_by = "mmm"). A wtna network is accepted only with cluster_by = "mmm"; dissimilarity clustering refuses it with an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

k

The number of clusters, a whole number from 2 to one less than the number of sequences. Required.

cluster_by

The clustering algorithm. "pam" (default) and the hierarchical methods "ward.D2", "ward.D", "complete", "average", "single", "mcquitty", "median" and "centroid" are passed to build_clusters() as its method; "mmm" fits a mixed Markov model with build_mmm() instead.

dissimilarity

The distance between sequences for dissimilarity clustering, one of those build_clusters() accepts. Default "hamming". Giving it with cluster_by = "mmm" raises an error.

...

Arguments for the two stages, routed by name. For dissimilarity clustering, build_clusters()'s na_syms, weighted, lambda, seed, q, p, covariates and estimator go to the clustering; with cluster_by = "mmm", build_mmm()'s n_starts, max_iter, tol, smooth, seed, covariates, covariate_effect and estimator go to the mixture fit. Everything else is meant for the network stage and must be an argument of build_network() or of a registered estimator; any other name raises an error before either stage runs. A name both stages accept goes to the clustering: under dissimilarity clustering a lambda given here is the Hamming decay of the clustering and never reaches an attention network, and the same holds for weighted. When data is a netobject, its stored build arguments are reused for the per-cluster networks, and a value given in the call replaces the stored one. The Details section lists which network arguments take effect.

Value

A netobject_group: one netobject per cluster, named "Cluster 1", "Cluster 2", and so on, with the clustering (a net_clustering, or for "mmm" a net_mmm_clustering) kept as its "clustering" attribute. print() names the clustering method and shows each cluster's network size, weight range and share of the sequences; cluster_diagnostics() reads the clustering, and summary() (the networks' metrics, a column per cluster), bootstrap_network() and net_centrality() take the group as it is.

Details

method, the estimators' own arguments (such as n_gram or direction) and build_network()'s threshold, scaling, start, end and params reach the per-cluster networks. A netobject input of the same method also passes on its estimator settings ($params, such as an attention network's lambda) unless params is given. With cluster_by = "mmm" and the default relative networks, which are the fitted chains, scaling and threshold are applied to the fitted weights, and an estimator argument, start, end or a new params raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input. For a one-hot netobject the stored build arguments are not used. Under "mmm", rebuilding a network built from long-format data with any method other than "relative" currently raises an error, because its column names are passed on to the wide per-cluster data.

See also

build_clusters, cluster_mmm, build_network

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","C","A","B"), V2 = c("B","C","A","B","A"),
                   V3 = c("C","A","B","C","B"))
grp <- cluster_network(seqs, k = 2)
grp
#> Group Networks (2 clusters via pam / hamming)
#> 
#>   Group      Nodes  Edges  Weights         N
#>   Cluster 1  3      2      [1.000, 1.000]  2 (40.0%)
#>   Cluster 2  3      4      [0.500, 1.000]  3 (60.0%)
# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 50, TRUE), V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 50, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 50, TRUE), V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 50, TRUE)
)
# Default: PAM clustering, relative (transition) networks
grp <- cluster_network(seqs, k = 3)


# MMM-based clustering
grp <- cluster_network(seqs, k = 2, cluster_by = "mmm")
# }
